item.title: Create Lambda Function for DynamoDB Integration
item.description:
We will build a Lambda function that acts as the API Backend responsible for receiving the hero_id parameter sent from the browser, querying DynamoDB, and returning the JSON result.

Step Action Technical Details
1 Access AWS Console Search for the Lambda service in the search bar.
2 Initialize Function Select Functions from the left menu > Click the orange Create function button.
3 Basic Configuration Select Author from scratch. Function name: dota2-backend-api. Runtime: Select Python 3.9 (or newer).
4 Configure Permissions Expand Change default execution role > Select Create a new role with basic Lambda permissions (AWS will automatically create a secure basic Role). Click Create function.
5 Attach DynamoDB Read Permissions Go to the Configuration tab > Permissions section > Click the blue Role name link. The system will open the IAM tab.
6 Add Inline Policy Click Add permissions > Create inline policy > Select the JSON tab and paste the code below (Remember to replace YOUR_ACCOUNT_ID) > Set policy name: DynamoDB_Read_Dota2_Metrics > Click Create policy.
7 Write API Source Code Return to the Lambda Function tab > Scroll down to the Code editor, clear the default code, paste the Python Backend code below > Click the orange Deploy button.

item.title: Configure HTTP API Gateway Ingress
item.description:
We proceed to set up an API Gateway endpoint to expose the Backend Lambda function as a public URL endpoint on the Internet.

Step Action Technical Details
1 Open API Gateway Search for the API Gateway service in the AWS Console.
2 Select API Type Find HTTP API > Click the orange Build button (HTTP APIs are faster and significantly cheaper than REST APIs).
3 Configure Integrations Click Add integration > Select Lambda. Select Region ap-southeast-1 > In the Lambda function field, select dota2-backend-api > Enter API name: dota2-public-api > Click Next.
4 Configure Routes Configure routes: Method: select GET. Path: enter /metrics. Target: keep the Lambda function. Click Next.
5 Keep Default Stage Under Stages, keep the default $default (Auto-deploy enabled). Click Next.
6 Complete Click Create. The system provides an Invoke URL string formatted as https://xxxx.execute-api.ap-southeast-1.amazonaws.com.
7 Test the API Copy the Invoke URL into your browser and append: /metrics?hero_id=74. If the screen returns a JSON response like {"hero_id": 74, "win_rate": "52.4"}, you are 100% successful!

item.title: Deploy Frontend UI to S3 Static Hosting
item.description:
We will deploy the static website interface source code (HTML/JS) to a dedicated S3 Bucket configured with Static Website Hosting.

Step Action Technical Details
1 Create UI Bucket Go to S3 Console, create a new bucket named: dota2-frontend-site-yourname.
2 Disable Block Public Access Because this is a public website, under Block Public Access, UNCHECK the Block all public access box. Click Create bucket.
3 Configure Web Hosting Open the newly created Bucket > Select the Properties tab > Scroll down to the Static website hosting section > Click Edit > Select Enable.
4 Specify Default File In the Index document field, enter index.html. Click Save changes. The system provides a website endpoint URL at the bottom of this section.
5 Create Local Source On your local machine, create a file named index.html and paste the HTML/JS code block below into it. (Remember to replace the API_GATEWAY_URL variable with your Invoke URL obtained in step 5.2).
6 Upload File to S3 Return to S3 Console > Objects tab > Click Upload and upload the index.html file.
7 Configure Bucket Policy Switch to the Permissions tab > Under Bucket policy > Click Edit and paste the JSON policy below to grant public read access > Click Save changes.
